title: Rational Canonical Form — Mathlib formalization connection (nonderogatory case)

problemStatement.formal: \forall K \text{ field}, \forall n, \forall M \in M_n(K), \text{IsNonderogatory}(M) \Rightarrow \exists P \in GL_n(K), P^{-1} M P = C(\mu_M)
problemStatement.plain: Every nonderogatory matrix is similar to its companion matrix — the nonderogatory case of the rational canonical form, formalized as a stand-alone theorem because Mathlib v4.26.0 does not have a general RCF.
whyMatters: Closes the cyclic-vector / RCF chain begun in cayley-hamilton-cyclic-vector-all-fields-oq-01.
Provides a concrete similarity matrix (the Krylov matrix) — not just an abstract similarity.
Stepping-stone toward a future Mathlib contribution adding companion matrices and RCF.

insights: Mathlib v4.26.0 has SmithNormalForm and module-structure theorems but NO matrix-form RCF or companionMatrix API. This entry's companionMx + nonderogatory_similar_to_companion seeds a future contribution.
The Krylov matrix P[i,j] = (M^j v)_i is the natural change-of-basis: invertibility of P is exactly cyclicity recast in matrix language.

The conjugation identity M·P = P·C(minpoly) decomposes column-by-column. Non-last columns give the trivial M·(M^j v) = M^{j+1} v. The last column reduces to the Cayley-Hamilton relation M^n v = -∑ c_k M^k v.
hMn_axiom is NOT a deep statement — it is routine: aeval M (minpoly K M) = 0 plus monicity gives M^n + ∑ c_k M^k = 0, hence M^n = -∑ c_k M^k. Applying mulVec v finishes.

The file imports CayleyHamiltonCyclicVectorAllFields (parent, gives existence of v) and CayleyHamiltonCyclicVectorAllFieldsOQ01OQ01 (gives minpoly_natDegree_of_cyclic which establishes natDegree = n).

Honest reading of the slug 'Rational canonical form Mathlib formalization connection': the answer to 'is RCF in Mathlib?' is no. The productive operationalization is to formalize the nonderogatory case as a stand-alone theorem, which the file does.

Session 6: monic + monic + equal natDegree + dvd ⇒ equal — write `b = a · c`, force `c.natDegree = 0` from natDegree-additivity, force `c.leadingCoeff = 1` from leadingCoeff-multiplicativity + monicity, conclude `c = 1`. About 12 lines of Mathlib API plumbing.
Session 6: `Polynomial.Monic` is definitionally `p.leadingCoeff = 1`, so `hp_monic : p.Monic` can be used as a `rw` rule against `p.leadingCoeff` directly. No `Monic.def.mp` needed.

Session 6: With S5's `aeval_companionMx_p_eq_zero` + S3's `companionMx_isCyclic_e0` + sibling OQ-01-OQ-01's `minpoly_natDegree_of_cyclic`, the minpoly identity falls out in 3 self-evident steps. The hardest part of the OQ-01-OQ-02 chain was the matrix-level Cayley-Hamilton (S5).
